item.title: Bank of Canada raises the policy rate by 25 basis points to 2½%

rating.summary: The Bank of Canada raised its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, citing persistently elevated inflation around 3% driven by high energy prices and building cost pressures. The Bank revised up its inflation outlook, now expecting CPI to average 3% in 2027 before returning to 2% by mid-2028. While acknowledging excess supply and trade uncertainties, the Bank signaled a cautious tightening bias with the possibility of further rate increases.
rating.stance_rationale: The decision to hike and the explicit signal that 'there could be a need to increase the policy rate further' reflects a moderately hawkish stance, tempered by language around proceeding 'carefully' given uncertainties and still-present excess supply in the economy.
key_quotes: There could be a need to increase the policy rate further, but given uncertainties, Governing Council agreed to proceed carefully.
Governing Council decided to increase the policy rate to reduce the risk that continuing high energy prices spread broadly to the prices of other goods and services.
